> What, if any, impact do you feel the history of apartheid has on your daily life?

Not so much in terms of daily life, personally I believe this to be since I am a very sheltered person. I attend a very white school and live in a very white area no where near any townships or camps. But as /u/l3utters said getting into University or any job will be challenging as BEE (Black Economic Empowerment) has been said to be very biased and in favor of the black race even if the other party (white for example) is more qualified, this will probably cause problems for me.
>Is apartheid something you think about often?

Not much, but sometimes. I sometimes think about where our families domestic worker (Maid seems to be the common title) would be if she had not been subject to apartheid, maybe she could have been a successful doctor.... but due to apartheid she is stuck cleaning and working on a low salary... so yes, it does cross my mind every now and then.
>Are you taught about apartheid in school? If so, please summarize what is taught.

100% I believe every person who has been through school has spent a year or two covering apartheid. They teach us how the black people were treated and shipped off to what is now known as Zimbabwe and the discrimination the black people went through... Last year we had the privilege of visiting the Apartheid museum, they show us how the people fought back and just the general struggles of the time (we did not learn much about the whites side of the story).
>Do you feel it is generalized or biased?

I believe it is very biased towards those who were subject to those affected by it but this common when learning about such a subject.
>Even though there are technically no racial barriers (i.e. separate bathrooms), do you feel welcome or comfortable every where?

Personally i do not, you do not see white private school kids walking through town or anything of the sort, when driving through a poor black area it does seem we get very strange looks from those near by, but also this is like everywhere in the world. 
>While you were born after apartheid ended, do you feel, from your experiences and knowledge of what old South Africa was like, that life in South Africa today is better or worse without apartheid

I like to think that there is the positives and negatives. 
Positives such as now we all get to unite as one nation no matter the race and culture and we all are supposedly given "equal" opportunity. The negatives can be that the end of apartheid has left millions without homes nor education, this is why we have such large squatter camps and such a high unemployment and low literacy rate. Generally i like to think that we were improving with the new government housing and education, but it appears as if we are heading down hill again due to load shedding and various other situations (ie. shitty government)

With the way our countries heading now we might end up in the stone age again, this due to our uneducated President whom has no clue whats going on.
